title: Back off and park assignments that repeatedly fail setup after containment
goal: After per-task containment landed in the runner dispatch loop (case study: task db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20, the runDispatchLoop catch around executeAssignment in runner/daemon.js), a task whose worktree setup persistently throws is interrupt-released and immediately reclaimable with zero backoff: the loop re-polls at once and can reclaim the same poisoned task forever, burning runner capacity and churning logs (the accepted residual risk in that task review; only deterministic git failures get the one-poll backoff and three-strikes backend parking added by task 1cae113f). Generalize the protection to the contained-catch path: add runner-side consecutive-failure backoff for the interrupt-released task (for example, abstain from reclaiming the same task and stage for N poll cycles with a logged reason) and extend backend streak parking beyond git failures so a task that fails setup repeatedly in place is parked until an operator retries, resumes, or moves it. Acceptance: a new runner test proves the loop does not immediately reclaim a task that just threw during setup; a backend test proves repeated setup-failure releases park the task; a single transient failure still retries promptly.
